blockers.quote: Last line inside the image: the next time you price something, price it in hours
blockers.why: Check #12 fails: the last spoken line is a lesson, a direction to the viewer about how to live. It isn't one real line inside the last image. It also sits against the rule that health topics never advise.
blockers.fix: End on a line that belongs to the bench and pays off the bus-pass tease from beat 4: "Six o'clock. He's teasing you about the bus pass again. You let him." (warm, low, unhurried). Nothing after it except the end card. The 'time, not money' idea stays in the picture: the laptop shut, nothing priced.

suggestions.quote: every job is the same trade at a lower price
suggestions.fix: This reads like an essay. Speak it as fragments with a finished landing: "Money comes back. Years don't. Every job, same trade. Cheaper." Direction: hushed, then dry.

suggestions.quote: It's one year. I'll earn it back.
suggestions.fix: Direction for the voice: light, confident, a little amused, so the turn at 78% can break it in the same words but quiet and hushed.

suggestions.quote: health costs and household poverty in India, then the hours a full-time job buys in a year
suggestions.fix: Two fact lines in a row. Put a beat of the father between them, and give each number its spoken form in say.yaml: "fifty-five million families a year" (pending G2 check), and the hours as words, e.g. "about two thousand hours" once sourced.
Say it as the app's voice, curious and low: "What if you could sell one year of your life?" Then answer at once with the thumb moving to the button, not a pause.
If this tag is ever voiced, add to say.yaml: "$100,000" -> "a hundred thousand dollars"; "1 crore" -> "one crore".

suggestions.quote: a nurse asks which of you is the patient
suggestions.fix: Keep the nurse's line a bubble of four words or fewer: "Which one's the patient?" Narrator stays silent over the picture, so it doesn't narrate what the shot already shows (#11).
